description: Multidisciplinary team interested in building a strong, practical solution around space, AI, software, and emerging technologies. We already have the core team covered and are mainly using this page for coordination.
summary:
TerraPulse is an open-source, multi-hazard Earth observation atlas and SAR analysis platform built for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge ("Dancing with the SARs"). It brings together NASA NISAR products (GCOV, GUNW, GOFF), NASA GIBS, EONET, COOLR, LHASA, ARIA, and ITS_LIVE alongside ESA Sentinel-1/Copernicus DEM, USGS, GDACS, GLIMS, WGMS, and OpenStreetMap into a single interactive web map and serverless API.

Instead of treating radar as just visual imagery, TerraPulse separates and exposes distinct scientific workflows: (1) Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) monitoring across five real lakes (253 Sentinel-1 radar epochs, ITS_LIVE glacier velocity, and repeat Pléiades terrain change); (2) post-event landslide scar screening powered by an ONNX-exported U-Net ensemble trained on Landslide4Sense, paired with live NASA LHASA forecasts and bounded OpenStreetMap exposure screening; and (3) global hazard catalogs and dated NISAR/MODIS case comparisons (floods in Mozambique and Algeria, earthquakes in Venezuela, and Pine Island Glacier). By keeping units, observation dates, and missing data explicit, TerraPulse makes complex multi-sensor hazard evidence accessible without overclaiming predictive certainty.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

TerraPulse combines an interactive global hazard map with reproducible machine-learning backends and serverless API endpoints (/api/glof, /api/landslide, /api/forecast, /api/exposure, and /api/chat):

  1. Multi-Hazard Global Map & Case Comparisons:
    • Global Catalogs & Live Feeds: Displays live and historical USGS earthquakes (by time window, magnitude, and depth), GDACS flood alerts, NASA EONET natural events (volcanoes, wildfires, storms, floods, landslides, drought), NASA COOLR landslide reports, WGMS glacier mass-balance records, GEM active faults, and PB2002 tectonic plate boundaries.
    • Dated Satellite & NISAR Cases: Lets users inspect and swipe-compare dated observations, including Lower Limpopo (Mozambique) MODIS 7/2/1 and NASA LANCE VIIRS 3-day flood layers linked to NISAR GCOV granules; Northern Venezuela numeric NASA JPL ARIA / NISAR GUNW line-of-sight displacement with USGS ShakeMap contours; Pine Island Glacier NISAR radar, GOFF, and ICESat-2 context; and Guelma / Lake Réghaïa (Algeria) NISAR Worldview comparisons.
    • Find NISAR & Natural-Language Assistant: Queries NASA Earthdata CMR granules and NASA COOLR polygons by coordinates, map click, or Open-Meteo place search, and includes an interactive assistant that executes catalog filters, layer switches, and case comparisons.
    • Monitors five high-mountain lakes (South Lhonak, Imja Tsho, Tsho Rolpa, Palcacocha, and Suicide Basin) in both normal and expert views.
    • Combines 253 Sentinel-1 C-band RTC radar epochs (2022–2024) segmented by an XGBoost water model (trained on 446 Sen1Floods11 chips across 11 leave-one-event-region-out folds; pooled IoU 0.5863, F1 0.7392 vs. 0.4561 IoU for the strongest tuned terrain baseline), 2024 NASA MEaSUREs ITS_LIVE annual glacier velocity, and dated CNES-derived Pléiades repeat-terrain surface change at South Lhonak (with an offline CPU reproduction script verifying the 0.5724 km² lake-area inference for 7 October 2023).
    • Links dated lake outlines and historical GLIMS/NRSC/JRC context directly onto the main map alongside quality grades, missing-data gaps, and downloadable JSON/CSV/GeoTIFF assets.
    • Post-Event Scar Screening: Runs a CPU-hosted ONNX ensemble of two residual U-Nets (14-band Sentinel-2 + ALOS terrain inputs, trained on Landslide4Sense; held-out 80-chip test AP 0.691, F1 0.662 at validation-selected threshold) to display true-positive/false-positive/false-negative overlays and heuristic review-priority tiers.
    • Rainfall-Triggered Forecast: Retrieves 30-arcsecond tiles from NASA LHASA Hazard Tomorrow for any coordinate within 60°S–60°N.
    • Buildings & Human Exposure: Executes bounded, user-triggered OpenStreetMap Overpass queries (with Geofabrik .poly coverage-aware regional routing for Europe and North America, global fallbacks, and caching) to summarize nearby buildings, roads, and amenities.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • All-Weather Disaster Visibility: SAR penetrates cloud cover and darkness, enabling flood and glacial-lake monitoring during monsoons and severe storms when optical imagery fails.
  • Decision Support Without Black-Box Overclaiming: Emergency analysts, researchers, and students can inspect raw dates, units, coverage gaps, and model limitations side by side rather than mistaking an image overlay for a calibrated risk score.
  • Accessible & Reproducible: Visitors can explore the full atlas, run held-out ML examples, and inspect real GLOF inferences directly in the browser or locally without needing paid cloud accounts or GPUs at inference time.

Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Frontend: HTML5, CSS, JavaScript (ES modules), React 19, Vite 8, Leaflet 1.9.4, MapLibre GL JS, D3-Geo, and TopoJSON Client.
  • Backend & Deployment: Python standard-library HTTP/serverless functions (api/landslide.py, api/glof.py, api/forecast.py, api/exposure.py, api/chat.py), Vercel serverless functions, and GitHub Actions CI.
  • Machine Learning & Geospatial Processing: PyTorch (residual U-Net training), ONNX Runtime (CPU inference), XGBoost, scikit-learn, NumPy, SciPy, Rasterio, Shapely, PyProj, h5py, Pillow, Matplotlib, earthaccess, and Google Earth Engine (Sentinel-1 GRD export script).
  • Hardware: Model training (Landslide4Sense U-Net ensemble and Sen1Floods11 XGBoost water model) ran on NVIDIA L40 GPUs; production inference and static/API serving run on standard CPU environments.

Creativity & Key Design Factors Considered

  • Strict Separation of Scientific Quantities: Rather than blending incompatible metrics into a single opaque "risk index," TerraPulse explicitly separates surface water area (km²), glacier speed (m/yr), surface elevation change (m), post-event landslide scars, LHASA rainfall-triggered forecasts, and OSM infrastructure exposure—and reminds users that water level and breach probability remain unmeasured without in-situ or bathymetric data.
  • Honest Handling of Missing Data & Cross-Sensor Boundaries: Unresolved pixels (such as radar layover/shadow, ambiguous zero-fill in ARIA displacement grids, or 47 unresolved Suicide Basin epochs) remain null or transparent gaps rather than being silently filled as zero. Similarly, the C-band Sentinel-1 water classifier is never blindly applied to L-band NISAR HH or S-band imagery.
  • Resilient, Offline-First Architecture: Heavy scientific processing and asset preparation run offline with SHA-256 provenance manifests; Overpass exposure lookups route by verified Geofabrik extract coverage and treat provider timeouts as unavailable rather than "zero buildings at risk"; and bundled Blue Marble/catalog snapshots ensure the map opens reliably even under limited connectivity.
